newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CAPRIATI BEATS SELES TO REACH CHICAGO FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CAPRIATI BEATS SELES TO REACH CHICAGO FINAL.

text.p: Jennifer Capriati revived her game and an old rivalry on Saturday when she upset top-ranked Monica Seles in the semifinals of the $450,000 Ameritech Cup to reach a tournament final for the first time since 1993.

Capriati, on the comeback trail after being out of the game for two years because of personal problems and injuries, beat Seles 6-3 6-3 and will face Jana Novotna in Sunday's final. Novotna staged a comeback herself in her 7-5 6-4 semifinal win over Swiss teen Martina Hingis.
"She clearly played a better match than I did," Seles said of Capriati, whom she last played in the French Open in 1992.
It will be Capriati's first final since the Canadian Open in 1993. Her last win was at Sydney earlier that year.
"More than anything, I did this for myself," Capriati said of her comeback. "It was for me, self satisfaction."

The two exchanged service breaks in the first four games of the first set, each sticking to her trademark baseline style. Capriati broke Seles again in a key seventh game, although Seles was at set point twice, and won the set with a break at 15.
Seles, who shares the world number one ranking with Steffi Graf, struggled in the second set, scoring just one point off Capriati's serve in her last four games.

For Capriati, ranked 50th in the world, even reaching the semifinals was an accomplishment. The 20-year-old American was a late entry into the Chicago event and was unseeded. She had yet to get past the quarter-finals this year.

Seles's comeback after being stabbed in the back in Hamburg in 1993 has been more successful, including a win this year at the Australian Open. But she had been bothered by a sore left shoulder since then, and this event was her first test after a month of extensive rehabilitation.
"I really think the therapy is working, so it's not even on my mind," Seles said.
Capriati has lost twice to Novotna this year, at Essen and Zurich, both times in the quarter-final round.
"This whole week I've felt myself play well and I just wanted to keep this up," Capriati said. "This is what I've been working for, working to see if I could be up there again and play good tennis."
In the other semifinal, Hingis was at set point three times in the first set and had a 4-1 lead in the second set, yet Novotna overcame both. She broke Hingis in the ninth and 11th games.
The 16-year-old threw her racket in frustration towards the net at the end of the 11th game and was assessed a violation by the chair umpire.
In the second set, Novotna halted play after three games to receive treatment for a blister on her left foot and to have her right knee taped.
Hingis opened a 4-1 lead, yet Novotna aggressively attacked the net and fired a series of forehand winners, scoring 20 of the next 23 points, including the final 13, to win the match.

"It was an unbelievable comeback," said Novotna, who had beaten Hingis in the final at Zurich last month. "I wasn't really aggressive enough in the beginning of the first set and I thought she was passing me well. I just started to fight back and that's what I did."
Hingis, number eight in the world, confessed to being tired from her singles and doubles matches late Friday, saying she will limit her doubles play in the future.
"I couldn't move my legs any more," the 16-year-old Swiss said. "I knew she couldn't move that well but I couldn't move either."
